clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old woman presented with left ear discharge, decreased hearing, and non-pulsatile tinnitus for four months, with a history of chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis and stroke causing left facial palsy and hemiparesis. Clinical examination revealed a central wet tympanic membrane perforation and left central facial palsy. Audiological assessment confirmed left conductive hearing loss. Flexible nasopharyngoscopy showed a bulge in the left nasopharyngeal wall without a mass. A CT angiography of the head and neck was ordered and performed to evaluate a suspected vascular lesion. The ear infection resolved after oral and topical ciprofloxacin. However, a validated and safe CT angiography report excerpt explicitly describing the left petrous internal carotid artery dissection aneurysm, which is the known final diagnosis, was not available in the disclosed evidence.
